elements.evidence: The added operative language permits Customer to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires “30 days' prior written notice to Vendor.”

elements.element: Customer receives a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees following convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Vendor must refund prepaid Fees covering the period after the effective termination date, which operates as a pro-rata refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that Vendor has no right to terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term.
The added operative language grants Customer a convenience-termination right for the Agreement or any Order Form.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires between 60 and 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires only 30 days' notice, which is outside the fallback range of 60–90 days.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee charged to Customer does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no early-termination fee, so the fee-cap condition is not triggered.

elements.element: If Vendor has a termination-for-convenience right, it may be exercised only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The clause prohibits Vendor from terminating for convenience during a committed term and grants no broader Vendor convenience-termination right.

elements.element: If Vendor has a termination-for-convenience right, Vendor must provide 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered language does not grant Vendor a termination-for-convenience right, so the notice condition is not triggered.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the preferred position: a Customer convenience right on 30 days' written notice, a post-termination refund of prepaid Fees, and no Vendor convenience right during a committed term. The fallback is not fully satisfied because the Customer notice period is 30 days rather than 60–90 days. The addition is targeted and leaves the existing cause-based termination rights unchanged.
